name: weak
description: No requirements or numbers, buzzwords, and can't answer basic follow-ups.
log: [00:05] Interviewer: "Hi, I'm Sam. Today let's design a URL shortener, like bit.ly, that handles 100 million new links a day. Where would you like to start?"
[00:20] Candidate: "Okay so I'd use microservices, with Kafka and Kubernetes so it scales."
[00:50] Interviewer: "Before the technology, what does the system need to do?"
[01:30] Interviewer: "How many requests a second are we talking about?"
[02:30] Whiteboard: added box "Kafka"; added box "Kubernetes"; added box "NoSQL"
[03:00] Interviewer: "Walk me through what happens when someone creates a link."
[03:10] Candidate: "It goes to Kafka, and then a service picks it up and saves it in NoSQL."
[03:40] Interviewer: "And how is the short code made?"
[03:50] Candidate: "Um, I'm not sure. Maybe random?"
[04:30] Interviewer: "What about when someone visits a short link?"
[04:40] Candidate: "It also goes through Kafka, then the service finds it."
[05:10] Interviewer: "Wouldn't a queue add latency to a redirect?"
[05:20] Candidate: "Kafka is really fast, so it's fine."
[07:00] Interviewer: "What happens if two random codes are the same?"
